'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Israel–Hamas war]]
**[[Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Israel–Hamas war]]
***At least seven [[Palestinians]] are killed during an [[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli military]] raid in [[Jenin]] in the [[West Bank]] that targeted a building that several [[Palestinian political violence|militants]] had [[barricade]]d themselves in. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/four-palestinians-killed-israeli-offensive-west-banks-jenin-ministry-says-2024-07-05/ (Reuters)]
**[[Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip (2023–present)|Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip]]
***A review article published in the [[medical journal]] ''[[The Lancet]]'' estimates the total death toll of Palestinians in Gaza to be at least 186,000 compared to the currently reported number of 38,000, around 8% of Gaza's pre-war population. This is attributed to the lack of reporting for indirect deaths, as well as the lack of operating hospitals and officials to report those deaths. [https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(24)01169-3/fulltext (''The Lancet'')] [https://www.npr.org/2024/02/29/1234159514/gaza-death-toll-30000-palestinians-israel-hamas-war (NPR)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Sennar offensive]]
***The [[Rapid Support Forces]] captures [[Dinder, Sudan|Dinder]], [[Sudan]] again, after it was briefly recaptured by the [[Sudanese Armed Forces|SAF]] on 4 July. The town was first captured by the RSF on 2 July. [https://sudantribune.com/article287874/ (''Sudan Tribune'')]
*[[Kivu conflict]]
**[[M23 offensive (2022–present)|M23 offensive]]
***[[March 23 Movement|M23]] rebels and the [[Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|FARDC]] agree to a two-week humanitarian truce proposed by the [[United States]]. The positions of the two groups are separated by about 1 kilometre in [[Matembe]]. Access to many areas remains difficult for humanitarians. [https://www.radiookapi.net/2024/07/07/actualite/securite/les-fardc-et-le-m23-respectent-la-treve-humanitaire-recommandee-par (Radio Okapi)]

'''Business and economy'''
*The [[European Union]] imposes [[tariff]]s on [[China|Chinese]] [[Electric vehicle industry in China|electric vehicles]] of up to 37.6%, prompting the [[Government of China|Chinese]] [[Ministry of Commerce (China)|Ministry of Commerce]] to investigate possible [[Trade war|retaliatory tariffs]] on European pork and [[brandy]] imports. [https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/china-urges-eu-take-talks-seriously-ev-tariffs-go-into-effect-2024-07-05/ (Reuters)]
*The [[Cabinet of Germany]] agrees on a 2025 [[Federal budget of Germany|budget plan]], averting collapse of the current cabinet following party disagreements and pressure from [[Alliance 90/The Greens|The Greens]] to forego its "[[German balanced budget amendment|debt brake]]" to increase emergency borrowing for [[List of military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War|Ukraine aid]]. [https://apnews.com/article/germany-budget-agreement-stimulus-coalition-a95dbc1d92c70ee2c10e921b8a5e0762 (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Hurricane Beryl]]
**Hurricane Beryl makes landfall on the [[Yucatán Peninsula]] in [[Mexico]] after killing 12 people in the [[Caribbean]]. [https://apnews.com/article/hurricane-beryl-tulum-mexico-resort-4b84e981f62bd53340a385fac42579f5 (AP)]
*At least 89 people are killed and dozens are missing after a boat carrying migrants capsized off the coast of [[Mauritania]]. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/north-africa/2024/07/05/89-migrants-dead-at-sea-off-mauritania (Al Arabiya)]
*Ten people are killed and 42 others are injured when a [[bus crash]]es into a bridge in [[São Paulo (state)|São Paulo state]], [[Brazil]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/least-10-dead-after-bus-crash-brazils-sao-paulo-state-2024-07-05/ (Reuters)]
*Five people are killed and 83 others are injured by a [[tornado]] in the [[Provinces of China|province]] of [[Shandong]], [[China]]. [https://apnews.com/article/china-shandong-heze-tornadoes-killed-injured-3f52c1df43f26696f4a72ef32e4489a9 (AP)]
*The [[Mount Etna]] and [[Stromboli#Volcano|Mount Stromboli]] [[volcano]]es on the [[Italy|Italian]] island of [[Sicily]] erupt, forcing a temporary closure of [[Catania–Fontanarossa Airport]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/7/5/sicily-closes-airport-as-etna-and-stromboli-volcanoes-erupt (Al Jazeera)]
*A [[dam failure]] in [[Buru Regency]], [[Indonesia]], causes massive flooding. [https://www.cnnindonesia.com/nasional/20240705211236-20-1118168/bendungan-waeapo-pulau-buru-maluku-jebol-rumah-warga-tenggelam (CNN Indonesia)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Peace negotiations in the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Russia–Hungary relations]], [[2024 peace missions by Viktor Orbán]]
***[[Prime Minister of Hungary|Hungarian Prime Minister]] [[Viktor Orbán]] meets with [[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] in [[Moscow]], [[Russia]], after meeting with [[President of Ukraine|Ukrainian President]] [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] on Tuesday, prompting condemnation among [[European Union]] member states. [https://www.politico.eu/article/with-brussels-fuming-vladimir-putin-welcomes-viktor-orban-as-eu-leader/ (Politico)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Attempted assassination of Lee Jae-myung]]
**A district court in [[Busan]], [[South Korea]], sentences the perpetrator in the stabbing of [[National Assembly (Korea)|National Assembly]] member and former opposition leader [[Lee Jae-myung]] to 15 years in prison. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/7/5/man-who-stabbed-south-korea-opposition-leader-gets-15-years-in-jail (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Greece]] passes a law to allow a six-day work week for industries that operate on a 24-hour basis. Workers have the option of working an additional eight hours for 40% additional pay. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/greece-6-day-work-week/ (CBS News)] [https://www.npr.org/2024/07/05/nx-s1-5027839/greece-six-day-workweek-law (NPR)]
*[[Catholic Church|Catholic]] [[Archbishop]] [[Carlo Maria Viganò]] is found guilty of [[schism in Christianity|schism]] for denying the legitimacy of [[Pope Francis]] and rejecting the [[Second Vatican Council]], and is subsequently [[excommunication|excommunicated]] by the [[Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/papal-enemy-archbishop-vigano-found-guilty-schism-excommunicated-2024-07-05/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 United Kingdom general election]]
**[[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative]] [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Rishi Sunak]] concedes defeat to [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] leader [[Keir Starmer]], ending 14 years of Conservative [[Government of the United Kingdom|government]]. [https://news.sky.com/story/the-labour-party-has-won-this-general-election-sunak-concedes-defeat-13162921 (Sky News)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/videos/cye0pznxj4lo (BBC News)] 
**[[Keir Starmer]] formally becomes Prime Minister after accepting an invitation from [[Monarchy of the United Kingdom|King]] [[Charles III]] to form a majority government. [https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/politics/breaking-keir-starmer-officially-becomes-33176249 (''Mirror'')] [https://www.bbc.co.uk/newsround/articles/crge8ejw3xdo (BBC News)]
**[[Rachel Reeves]] is appointed as the UK's first ever female [[Chancellor of the Exchequer]] in the [[Starmer ministry]]. [https://www.itv.com/news/2024-07-05/honour-of-my-life-reeves-becomes-uks-first-female-chancellor-in-800-years (ITV News)]
*[[2024 Iranian presidential election]]
**A second round run-off is held between [[Iranian reformists|reformist]] [[Masoud Pezeshkian]] and [[Iranian Principlists#Factions|ultra conservative]] [[Saeed Jalili]] to become the 9th [[President of Iran]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-presidential-contenders-face-hurdle-voter-apathy-2024-07-02/ (Reuters)]
**[[Masoud Pezeshkian]] wins the Iranian presidential run-off. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/article/2024/jul/06/iran-reformist-masoud-pezeshkian-extends-lead-in-presidential-election-count (''The Guardian'')]
